answer: Each identity claims one island station and posts a 70-credit bond. A ferrous magnetometer keyed to that station files one magnetic reading each epoch. Auditors recompute the field from the island ledge survey table; a reading over 2 percent off burns the bond and revokes the station. The first gauge fee is 38 credits; the kth gauge pays 38+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7031 and 1000 fakes cost 3,534,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-gauge ring fails because one rented serial cannot sign readings for two stations. An honest operator pays 38 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
